current_evidence: The PDF at this stable URL now carries 'May 2026' on its cover and cites NPPF Dec 2024 and the Aug 2025 LNRS. It is the top search result, and no newer list was found on the council's planning pages, which do not link a list directly.

issues.detail: The List date 2026-05-01 is taken from PDF metadata. The document text says only 'May 2026', so the date basis should be the text and not the metadata.
issues.evidence: Cover: 'Leicestershire County Council Planning Application Validation Requirements / May 2026'

issues.detail: Many requirements from the Appendix 1 Local Validation Checklist are missing from app_type_rows. Hydrological/Hydrogeological Assessment (minerals and waste with dewatering or effects on the water table/surface water) is missing. National Forest (sites in the National Forest must show how planting will be accommodated) is missing. River Mease SAC HRA (development in the SAC catchment; foul and surface water drainage details) appears only as a fragment in tab_items. Sunlight/Daylight/Lighting Assessment is missing. Public Rights of Way (proposals affecting a PRoW, including temporary effects) is missing. Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment is missing. Economic Statement (new or lost employment uses) is missing. Aerodrome Safeguarding Assessment (near East Midlands Airport, and lighting, solar, wind and bird-attracting landscaping) is missing. Mineral Assessment (non-mineral development in a Minerals Safeguarding Area) is missing. Restoration and Aftercare (all mineral extraction) is missing. Statement of Community Involvement (major development) is missing. HMMP (where BNG applies) is missing. LNRS alignment statement / Statement of biodiversity impact is missing.

This is a county authority (minerals, waste and the council's own Reg 3 development). Grokbot placed all 27 requirements under 'Full planning' as 'INFERRED'. It left the 'Minerals & waste (county)' and 'County own devt (Reg 3)' rows as '(none) - national requirements only', although these are the only application types the list actually serves. Minerals-only items such as Restoration and Aftercare, Hydrological Assessment and vibration survey should sit under Minerals & waste.
issues.evidence: Para 3.0 'with all applications (unless otherwise stated)'; 4.27 and 4.82 apply to minerals/waste. The council's planning page says it deals with minerals, waste and its own developments.

issues.detail: Several tab_items are boilerplate or process text, not requirements. One is a footnote citation ('Available at: legislation.gov.uk [Accessed 8 September 2025]... Article 12'). Others are paper-copy and PDF format advice ('one paper copy', 'pdf is the recommended file format', 'page size should correspond to the print @ scale'). Another is the advisory line 'Although not a requirement of legislation, the inclusion of a linear scale bar is also useful'.

Several trigger excerpts are fragments that do not state when the requirement applies. Arboricultural row: 'a draft revision of BS 5837 has been published...' (the real trigger is work affecting trees or hedgerows on or adjacent to the site, para 4.37). Drainage row: text about carbon emissions. Environmental Statement row: text about the number of hard copies. Open space row: the Transport Assessment heading. CIL row: Reg 122 tests text (the county does not charge CIL). Odour/Dust/Vibration row: duplicates the noise paragraph. BNG row: starts mid-sentence 'exempt from BNG...'.
issues.evidence: Para 4.37 'Where a proposal involves work that affect any trees or hedgerows within or adjacent to the application site'

issues.detail: The Design and Access Statement row omits that waste development, material change of use, engineering and mining operations do NOT need a DAS. This exemption matters most for a minerals/waste authority.
issues.evidence: Para 3.16: 'Applications for waste development, a material change of use, engineering or mining operations do not need to be accompanied by a Design and Access Statement.'

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment row gives only the Flood Zones 2 and 3 trigger. It omits the Flood Zone 1 triggers: sites of 1 ha or more, critical drainage areas, areas flagged by a SFRA, and other flood sources where a more vulnerable use is introduced.
issues.evidence: Para 4.20 'In Flood Zone 1, an assessment should accompany all proposals involving: sites of 1 hectare or more;'

issues.detail: The Health Impact Assessment row quotes general aims. The actual trigger is HIA Screening for all major development, including minerals/waste, buildings of 1,000 m2 or more, and sites of 1 ha or more.
The Planning Obligations / Heads of Terms row omits the limiting condition that draft Heads of Terms are required only where LCC considers them essential and this was agreed at pre-application stage.

The 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' row is encouragement rather than a validation requirement. The 'CIL Additional Information / Form' row is not a requirement for this county authority.
issues.evidence: Para on pre-application discussions; CIL text quotes Reg 122 tests only

summary: Grokbot's link is the current May 2026 list. Its extraction misses about half of the 30+ Appendix 1 items, especially the minerals-specific ones. It also mis-files everything under Full planning while leaving the Minerals & waste and Reg 3 rows empty, and includes boilerplate text as requirements.
